data.gender_notes: Amandina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'amare' meaning 'to love'. Amandina is a Latin feminine name meaning 'beloved' or 'lovable'. In Christian tradition, it may also be associated with St. Amandina, a Roman martyr. The name Amandina carries the meaning “Beloved, Lovable” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Amandina usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved, lovable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine love and compassion
data.etymology: Amandina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beloved, Lovable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amandina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

It is a beautiful and melodic name that evokes feelings of love, tenderness, and affection. It is often given as a name to girls who are considered lovable or beloved. In some cultures, it may be used as a term of endearment towards a beloved family member or friend.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Amandina holds deep spiritual significance. It is a reminder of God's infinite love for his creation and his children. It is a call to love and serve God with all of one's heart and to strive to live a life that reflects God's love in all matters. Additionally, for those named Amandina, it can be seen as a reminder of their own value and worth as beloved children of God. The name can inspire a deep sense of personal devotion and dedication to God. It can also serve as a reminder of the Christian virtue of charity, to love and serve others as God loves and serves us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amandina: Enduring Love. A name derived from the Latin 'amare' to love, and 'dina' meaning powerful. This name embodies the strength and constancy of love, a reminder to cherish and uphold relationships with deep devotion.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Amandina was a 16th century Italian saint. The name Amandina carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Amandina was a member of the Capuchin Order and is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Amandina has gained popularity in some African countries, particularly in countries such as Angola and Mozambique. It is often given to girls and is associated with love, kindness, and strength.
